criteria.description: Executing a preflight check's remediation changes that check's state; checks with no possible remediation emit none and are declared exempt.
criteria.evidence: tests/architectural/test_remediation_effectiveness.py - 13 passed. Drives every remediation-emitting state in an isolated fixture, executes the emitted command, re-evaluates. Binds the operator-visible composed blocked_reason (C-EFF-3), not the returned field. Two states proven to have NO possible self-service remediation (every write path round-trips the YAML through the sole writer, INV-9) emit None and are declared exempt with identity pinned.
criteria.notes: Delivered narrower than a naive reading: 'every emitted remediation works, and states with no possible remediation emit none'. Recorded as analysis finding S1.

criteria.description: The blocked legacy-bundle charter state names a remediation that actually unblocks the operator.
criteria.evidence: tests/specify_cli/charter_freshness/test_sc002_walkthrough.py - SC-002 measured at 1 step on the F2 fixture. Red-first per NFR-002: WP01 landed the mechanism RED (4 failed / 9 passed on exactly the four `charter sync` states) before WP02 corrected anything; an independent reviewer verified the red at WP01's tip and the green at WP02's. Reviewer also mutation-tested the walkthrough - reverting to `charter sync` turns it red, so it walks the real gate->execute->re-run loop.

criteria.description: Remediation effectiveness is enforced structurally, not by author discipline.
criteria.evidence: The FR-001 mechanism is an AST-derived census over compute_freshness with pinned floors (5 remediation-emitting states + 2 exempt == 7 conserved total, 3 producers), plus an exemption-identity pin. Survived three separate coverage-shrink attacks during review: (1) drop a state and lower the floor, (2) keep the sum but swap an exempt member, (3) re-introduce the runner backfill. Each was demonstrated green-then-closed.
criteria.notes: C-001/DIRECTIVE_043: the class is closed, including R-006's second live instance on the runner's default path, not just the reported string.

criteria.description: Every operator-reachable surface returns the same answer to 'does the charter exist'.
criteria.evidence: tests/charter/test_charter_presence_seam.py - an src/-wide AST scan (not a curated root list) asserting every charter-presence resolver routes through the canonical non-mutating seam charter.bundle.charter_yaml_present. Falsification verified by two reviewers planting unrouted resolvers in src/specify_cli/dashboard/, src/specify_cli/status/ and src/runtime/next/_internal_runtime/ - all turned it RED with no list update. F2 fixture: gate, dashboard resolver and scanner all agree.
criteria.notes: Census revised six times (2->8->9->10->9->10); the final miss (the dashboard resolver) was invisible because _SCAN_ROOTS was itself a hand-written list. See R-003a.

criteria.description: 'No charter at all' is distinguishable from 'charter present but not in the required form'.
criteria.evidence: computer.py now emits a truthful detail on both `missing` branches naming exactly the legacy bundle files actually present, with singular/plural agreement. F1 reads 'this project has no charter at all'; F2 reads 'this project has a charter, just not in the required form'. A partial-bundle overclaim was caught in review (the detail named all four files when only one existed) and fixed with subset-specific tests.
criteria.notes: No new state value: the existing missing/invalid vocabulary was sufficient once detail carried the answer. cli.py needed zero changes.

criteria.description: A project with no charter at all keeps its advisory, non-blocking treatment.
criteria.evidence: tests/architectural/test_charter_blocking_envelope.py - four-shape blocking matrix measured against the pre-mission baseline and the mission tip, asserted per-shape (not only in aggregate). F1 proven non-blocking through the real gate path.
